look_here_first: Inspect several mature leaves from one branch: water oak commonly has a narrow wedge-shaped base and a broader, often shallowly three-lobed bristle-tipped apex. Confirm small second-year acorns in shallow cups.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native principally eastward in bottomland habitats; reviewed draft documents no confirmed project target-zone counties.

best_field_traits: variable small wedge- to spatula-shaped leaves, often widest near the tip
leaf apex frequently shallowly three-lobed with minute bristle tips
small acorns with shallow scaly cups; acorns mature in two seasons
deciduous to tardily deciduous bottomland red oak

comparisons.key_distinctions: Willow oak (Q. phellos) has consistently narrow, entire willow-like leaves rather than the typical widened or shallowly lobed water-oak tip. Shumard oak (Q. shumardii) has larger leaves with deeper pointed lobes and conspicuous sinuses. Laurel oak (Q. laurifolia) has mostly unlobed, more evenly elliptic leaves; check several leaves because water-oak leaves vary.

diagnostic_image_plan: several mature leaves from one twig showing shape variation and bristle tips
mature acorn and cup in close-up
